criterion: ccmorph probe on a profile whose gateway lists models with no published size and no catalogue entry says, under the profile's name, that it looked for context window sizes and found none, names the models, says the profile still works (at Claude Code's 200,000-token default) with the free and the paid fix, and exits 0, not 1. Proved by a Go stub test in ctxwindow/probe_test.go (go test ./ctxwindow/) and a fake-gateway test in tests/context_probe_cli_test.py (CI).
evidence: ctxwindow/report.go's ReportUnresolved prints "<profile>: looked for context window sizes for N models and found none:" with the sorted model list, "Neither the gateway nor the model catalogue publishes a size.", "The profile still works: Claude Code runs a model with no size at its 200,000-token default.", then the free `ccmorph context <profile> <model> <tokens>` before the paid `ccmorph probe <profile> --model <model> --allow-inference`. run()'s empty-values path in ctxwindow/probe_main.go now calls reportProfiles and returns 0 unless a Note says Failed. Proved by TestProbeSaysWhatItLookedForWhenNoSizeIsPublished (exact heading and model list, the 200,000 default, free before paid, exit 0; a profile with no api key exits 1) and TestReportUnresolvedOrdersTheFreeFixBeforeThePaidOne in ctxwindow/probe_test.go; both pass when run by name (the full package also starts fake gateways, which the sandbox refuses to bind, so CI runs it). TestMainArgumentsAndReporting keeps the old exit-1 status for a run that sized one model while another stayed unsized, and still exits 1 for a lookup that breaks, so a completed discovery cannot pass itself off as a result. Also pinned by test_a_gateway_with_no_sizes_says_what_it_looked_for_gh_371 (a gateway with no sizes at all: exit 0) and test_an_unsized_model_names_the_remedies_and_exits_one (a mixed run: the report says the profile still works, exit stays 1) in tests/context_probe_cli_test.py, fake-gateway tests that run in CI (they need a local port).

criterion: ccmorph probe prints one shape for its result on every profile: each result group starts with '<profile>: ' and says what it found about context window sizes (sizes saved, sizes already saved, no size found, a failed lookup), with detail lines indented under it, including in a sweep of two profiles; 'Nothing discovered.' is gone. Proved by a Go stub sweep test in ctxwindow/probe_test.go and the updated pins in tests/context_probe_cli_test.py.
evidence: reportProfiles in ctxwindow/report.go prints one group per tried profile, in order, each non-indented line starting "<profile>: "; Commit in ctxwindow/launch.go speaks the saved/already-saved groups and reportProfiles adds the failed-lookup, no-size and --check groups. run() calls reportProfiles on all three result paths (no values, --check, after Commit), and the old "Nothing discovered." block is deleted. --check saves nothing, so it now names each sized profile too: "gw: found context window sizes for 2 models; no changes." (or "N would change."). Proved by TestProbeReportsEveryProfileInOneShape in ctxwindow/probe_test.go: a sweep of gamma and work asserts every non-indented line starts "gamma: " or "work: ", the first run says "gamma: found context window sizes for 3 models; 3 saved for new sessions:" and the second "... all were already saved."; TestCheckSaysWhatItFoundWhenNothingChanged asserts the exact no-change group for a saved profile; both pass by name. The updated pins in tests/context_probe_cli_test.py (test_default_run_writes_declared_limits_and_says_what_changed, test_every_routed_profile_is_swept_when_none_is_named) hold the same lines, including the check group, and run in CI.

criterion: ccmorph probe --help (and probe <profile> --help, probe -i -h, the retired verb, and ccmorph help probe) prints one page that starts with 'Usage: ccmorph probe [profile] [options]', says what the command looks up in the words 'context window', and gives every option the probe accepts (every name in its parser, plus -i) one line with its meaning. Proved by tests/cli_messages_test.py and a Go test in cli/help_wrap_test.go that reads the option names from the parser.
evidence: cli/main.go answers helpAsked(rest) with l.usage("probe") before secureDirs, so every spelling of --help reaches the cli's page; usageTopics["probe"] begins "Usage: ccmorph probe [profile] [options]", says "context window", and gives each option one row. ProbeOptions in ctxwindow/probe_main.go is the list parseArgs iterates, so the page and the parser cannot drift. TestProbeHelpGivesEveryOptionOneLine in cli/help_wrap_test.go reads ctxwindow.ProbeOptions plus -i and requires, at widths 0 and 80, the Usage prefix, "context window", and exactly one row with a non-empty meaning per option; it passes with the other help tests under `go test ./cli/ -run 'Help|ProbeHelp'`. tests/cli_messages_test.py checks the same first line, "context window", and that `ccmorph probe --help` prints exactly what `ccmorph help probe` prints; `pytest tests/cli_messages_test.py -k 'probe or help_is_concise'` passed 6 tests here.

criterion: In a terminal 80 columns wide no line of probe's output or help page is wider than 80 cells, splits a word or model id, or leaves a closing bracket on a line of its own: the remedy commands are whole lines of their own and the model list and prose wrap at 80. Proved by Go tests that check every line of the issue's case, a long-profile/long-model-id case and the help page (ctxwindow/probe_test.go, cli/help_wrap_test.go).
evidence: wrapLine and reportWidth=80 in ctxwindow/report.go wrap the report, the model list, the remedy commands and the paid-probe warning at spaces with a hanging indent (a word wider than the line stays whole), and Commit in ctxwindow/launch.go puts an over-long model row on two lines rather than cropping it. TestProbeOutputFitsEightyColumns in ctxwindow/probe_test.go runs the report for a 33-character profile name with three 40-character model ids and asserts every line is at most 80 runes, every line's brackets balance and no line is a lone ")", every id is whole, and the commands fall back to <model> when they cannot fit; TestPaidProbeWarningFitsEightyColumns runs the paid warning with a 33-character profile and a 40-character model id and asserts every line is at most 80 runes with no split bracket and the warning's words intact; TestProbeSaysWhatItLookedForWhenNoSizeIsPublished checks the issue's three-model case. The help page is held to 80 by TestEveryHelpPageFitsEightyColumnsWithoutCuttingAWord (loops over usageTopics, so "probe" is included) and TestProbeHelpGivesEveryOptionOneLine at width 80 in cli/help_wrap_test.go, both passing under `go test ./cli/ -run 'Help|ProbeHelp'`. The fake-gateway tests in tests/context_probe_cli_test.py also assert every stderr line is at most 80 (test_a_gateway_with_no_sizes_says_what_it_looked_for_gh_371) and pin the wrapped paid warning; those run in CI.
